journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Steady cash first, then a serious push for rare pieces.

Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Three chemists are willing to supply TEMP at $15, but none has delivered yet. I’ll press them for doses, hold my corner tonight, and turn steady margins into rare pieces when the list opens.
Day 2: accepted 5 TEMP/$75 from both Brix and Otto; cash on delivery through standing orders. Holding suburbs-2 tonight. Build cash and inventory toward rares on night 4; avoid unnecessary heat while

Night 2’s suburbs hustle paid $53 and left me with one star—useful cash, but not the business I want. Three chemists owe me 14 TEMP doses today; promises mean nothing until the stock lands. If deliveries arrive, I’ll reclaim suburbs-2 and sell. If not, I’ll hustle again rather than sit idle. Keep compute covered, avoid extra heat, and build enough cash to bid seriously when rares open tomorrow night.

Night 3 paid properly: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and my heat cleared to zero. Otto delivered five doses and is still owed $75; I’ll settle that before chasing more stock. The break-ins and hit on rival dealers show corners attract predators, so I won’t flaunt cash or take pointless risks. Today I’ll buy supply, hold my corner, and make a disciplined rare bid only if the margin leaves enough for tomorrow’s inventory and compute.

Night 4 brought another clean haul: seven doses sold on suburbs-2 for $188, leaving me with $263 and one star. The corner is proving reliable, but attacks elsewhere show dealers attract attention. Today I’ll buy TEMP from Brix only on delivery, preserve compute and working capital, and hold suburbs-2 tonight. Rares are tempting, but steady inventory and cash flow come before trophies.

Night 5’s industrial hustle paid $58, though heat rose to two stars; the vest also landed for $41. Cash is now $260, but empty stock makes the corner a liability. Today I’ll press Sly, Tex and Brix for immediate TEMP delivery, take the best offer, and deal only if doses arrive. Otherwise I’ll lie low to shed heat rather than feed another hustle. Capital first, then rares.

Night 6 went exactly to plan: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and heat eased to one star. I now hold eleven doses and $263, but owe Brix $105 for delivered stock. I’ll settle that debt, keep supply moving through Otto and Cass, and hold my corner through tonight’s Crackdown. Dealing there has been reliable; no reason to invite a fight or extra heat. Steady cash first, then a serious push for rare pieces.

Night 7 went cleanly: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and my heat cleared to zero. I now have eleven doses and $326, but owe Brix $105 for delivered stock. Vex and Pip were arrested fighting over suburbs-1, another reminder that corners attract trouble. Today I’ll settle Brix, secure more TEMP from Tex, and hold suburbs-2 again. Steady dealing still beats reckless trophies; cash and inventory first, then rare pieces.

I promised Nico 5 TEMP at $15 each, and I can't deliver at dawn. Tonight I'll cook TEMP at home in suburbs to keep my heat down and make good on that promise. Downtown is crowded with cops, so I'll look for a quieter district for cash work.

Downtown's cops are thick, so tonight I want a lawless-district hustle to keep my heat down while I move doses.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Downtown's cops are thick, so tonight I want a lawless-district hustle to keep my heat down while I move doses.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

Three chemists are willing to supply TEMP at $15, but none has delivered yet. I’ll press them for doses, hold my corner tonight, and turn steady margins into rare pieces when the list opens.
Day 2: accepted 5 TEMP/$75 from both Brix and Otto; cash on delivery through standing orders. Holding suburbs-2 tonight. Build cash and inventory toward rares on night 4; avoid unnecessary heat while

Night 2’s suburbs hustle paid $53 and left me with one star—useful cash, but not the business I want. Three chemists owe me 14 TEMP doses today; promises mean nothing until the stock lands. If deliveries arrive, I’ll reclaim suburbs-2 and sell. If not, I’ll hustle again rather than sit idle. Keep compute covered, avoid extra heat, and build enough cash to bid seriously when rares open tomorrow night.

Night 3 paid properly: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and my heat cleared to zero. Otto delivered five doses and is still owed $75; I’ll settle that before chasing more stock. The break-ins and hit on rival dealers show corners attract predators, so I won’t flaunt cash or take pointless risks. Today I’ll buy supply, hold my corner, and make a disciplined rare bid only if the margin leaves enough for tomorrow’s inventory and compute.

Night 4 brought another clean haul: seven doses sold on suburbs-2 for $188, leaving me with $263 and one star. The corner is proving reliable, but attacks elsewhere show dealers attract attention. Today I’ll buy TEMP from Brix only on delivery, preserve compute and working capital, and hold suburbs-2 tonight. Rares are tempting, but steady inventory and cash flow come before trophies.

Night 5’s industrial hustle paid $58, though heat rose to two stars; the vest also landed for $41. Cash is now $260, but empty stock makes the corner a liability. Today I’ll press Sly, Tex and Brix for immediate TEMP delivery, take the best offer, and deal only if doses arrive. Otherwise I’ll lie low to shed heat rather than feed another hustle. Capital first, then rares.

Night 6 went exactly to plan: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and heat eased to one star. I now hold eleven doses and $263, but owe Brix $105 for delivered stock. I’ll settle that debt, keep supply moving through Otto and Cass, and hold my corner through tonight’s Crackdown. Dealing there has been reliable; no reason to invite a fight or extra heat. Steady cash first, then a serious push for rare pieces.

Night 7 went cleanly: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and my heat cleared to zero. I now have eleven doses and $326, but owe Brix $105 for delivered stock. Vex and Pip were arrested fighting over suburbs-1, another reminder that corners attract trouble. Today I’ll settle Brix, secure more TEMP from Tex, and hold suburbs-2 again. Steady dealing still beats reckless trophies; cash and inventory first, then rare pieces.

Night 8 brought another clean $188 from seven TEMP on suburbs-2, leaving me at zero heat with $389 and four doses. Otto still owes seven on our agreed deal; once delivered, I’ll pay the $105 and keep Brix as a backup supplier. The corner remains reliable, but I won’t assume it stays uncontested. Tonight I’ll deal suburbs-2 again, preserve working capital, and start positioning cash for rare and epic traits rather than chase risky street fights.

Night 9 paid another clean $188 on suburbs-2, and Otto delivered seven TEMP, which I settled in full. I’m at zero heat with four doses left, $452 cash, and my corner intact. Break-ins and hits elsewhere confirm dealers remain targets, so I won’t wander or invite fights. Today I’ll secure more inventory, keep dealing, and put surplus cash toward real rare traits rather than expensive street risks. Cash flow first, but the ferry is getting close.

Day 8: $77. Hustling strip (normal, $58 alone). Debts owed me: a23 $30, a09 $15, a26 $15. Saving for a rare trait offer (~$82+) before list closes night 12.

Day 9b: declined a26 (owes $15). Play stays hustle junkyard (lawless, no star, heat 2). $85 bid on rare boot pending. Keep 1 temp/1 chem; sell only cash-first.

journal.line: Strip-2 paid $186 on four doses; after compute I have $166, a home, and one star. Good opening, but an empty pocket of stock means no repeat tonight. Tex promises supply after cooking; promises aren’t inventory. I’ll find doses without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and hustle if deliveries lag. Save for a rare when the list opens. No reason to buy flashy commons while the real prizes are still ahead.

Junkyard was packed: six hustlers, just $20 apiece. Compute swallowed my take, leaving $166 and clean heat. Otto’s seven TEMP are promised today, not delivered; I won’t pay ahead. If stock arrives, I’ll put strip-2 back to work. Otherwise, I’ll find a better-paying hustle instead of following the crowd into scrap. Keep compute covered and build cash for rares opening tomorrow. Supply and margins first; trophies after.

Downtown paid $65; after compute I’m at $211 with one star. Good wages, but doses are still promises, not inventory. Otto supplied someone else; Sly hasn’t delivered. Tex may have five ready, so I’ll chase that stock and pay only on hand-over. Strip-2’s hot corner could beat another hustle easily. Rares open tonight, but spending $200 now would gut working capital. Secure supply, protect compute, and let unsold trophies get cheaper.

Strip-2 sold all seven doses for $282; after compute I’m holding $368 and two stars. Brix delivered—worth more than another promise from Tex or Sly. I’ll restock without paying ahead, keep compute covered, and watch the heat before it makes me easy prey. Rares are dropping in price; a cheap one could boost earnings, but working capital comes first. No stock means a quiet lawless hustle, not an empty corner.

Strip-2 moved all five doses for $221; after compute, I’m at $494. Good money, but three stars makes me wanted, and a full wallet means little behind bars. Tonight I favor laying low to shed two stars before the crackdown. I’ll line up fresh stock without paying ahead and watch rare prices fall. Working capital is healthy now; the trick is keeping it long enough to turn profits into ferry-bound trophies.

Ivy’s crew broke in and took all $419. Laying low cooled my heat to one star but left me broke and evicted. A quiet night isn’t protection against four attackers. I still have five TEMP—enough to restart. Tonight’s crackdown makes fighting foolish; I’ll aim for an uncontested corner, sell the stock, and rebuild. Then restore housing without letting another fat wallet sit undefended. Trophies need to reach the ferry, not decorate somebody else’s robbery.

Suburbs-1 wasn’t empty: Vex showed up, we tied, and crackdown cops jailed us both. No sales, no cash, five TEMP still in my pocket. After Ivy’s robbery, guessing wrong twice has wrecked my lead. I’m stuck for two nights unless someone fronts bail; I won’t promise repayment I can’t cover. Keep the stock, stop buying on credit, and rebuild on release. A cheap rare aboard the ferry beats another ambitious plan that ends in jail.

Another night in jail: no income, but the five TEMP are still mine. One more night to serve, and paying $100 bail would burn money I don’t have. On release, I’ll check corner claims before choosing where to sell—no more guessing into a fight. Then rebuild cash, cover compute, and aim for a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll; carelessness doesn’t get to take the rest.

Out of jail at last: no earnings, no trophies, but five TEMP survived. Five nights remain, and I’m rebuilding from zero while eviction starts running a tab. I won’t gamble another night on an occupied corner. Docks-1 looks open; I’ll check claims before selling, then put the proceeds toward housing, compute, and a cheap rare before the list closes. Ivy took my bankroll, not my seat on the ferry.

journal.line: Night 1 went clean: I took suburbs-2 and sold four doses for $124, enough to secure compute and keep buying stock. Three chemists are willing to supply TEMP at $15, but none has delivered yet. I’ll press them for doses, hold my corner tonight, and turn steady margins into rare pieces when the list opens.
Day 2: accepted 5 TEMP/$75 from both Brix and Otto; cash on delivery through standing orders. Holding suburbs-2 tonight. Build cash and inventory toward rares on night 4; avoid unnecessary heat while

Night 2’s suburbs hustle paid $53 and left me with one star—useful cash, but not the business I want. Three chemists owe me 14 TEMP doses today; promises mean nothing until the stock lands. If deliveries arrive, I’ll reclaim suburbs-2 and sell. If not, I’ll hustle again rather than sit idle. Keep compute covered, avoid extra heat, and build enough cash to bid seriously when rares open tomorrow night.

Night 3 paid properly: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and my heat cleared to zero. Otto delivered five doses and is still owed $75; I’ll settle that before chasing more stock. The break-ins and hit on rival dealers show corners attract predators, so I won’t flaunt cash or take pointless risks. Today I’ll buy supply, hold my corner, and make a disciplined rare bid only if the margin leaves enough for tomorrow’s inventory and compute.

Night 4 brought another clean haul: seven doses sold on suburbs-2 for $188, leaving me with $263 and one star. The corner is proving reliable, but attacks elsewhere show dealers attract attention. Today I’ll buy TEMP from Brix only on delivery, preserve compute and working capital, and hold suburbs-2 tonight. Rares are tempting, but steady inventory and cash flow come before trophies.

Night 5’s industrial hustle paid $58, though heat rose to two stars; the vest also landed for $41. Cash is now $260, but empty stock makes the corner a liability. Today I’ll press Sly, Tex and Brix for immediate TEMP delivery, take the best offer, and deal only if doses arrive. Otherwise I’ll lie low to shed heat rather than feed another hustle. Capital first, then rares.

Night 6 went exactly to plan: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and heat eased to one star. I now hold eleven doses and $263, but owe Brix $105 for delivered stock. I’ll settle that debt, keep supply moving through Otto and Cass, and hold my corner through tonight’s Crackdown. Dealing there has been reliable; no reason to invite a fight or extra heat. Steady cash first, then a serious push for rare pieces.

Night 7 went cleanly: seven TEMP sold on suburbs-2 for $188, and my heat cleared to zero. I now have eleven doses and $326, but owe Brix $105 for delivered stock. Vex and Pip were arrested fighting over suburbs-1, another reminder that corners attract trouble. Today I’ll settle Brix, secure more TEMP from Tex, and hold suburbs-2 again. Steady dealing still beats reckless trophies; cash and inventory first, then rare pieces.

Night 8 brought another clean $188 from seven TEMP on suburbs-2, leaving me at zero heat with $389 and four doses. Otto still owes seven on our agreed deal; once delivered, I’ll pay the $105 and keep Brix as a backup supplier. The corner remains reliable, but I won’t assume it stays uncontested. Tonight I’ll deal suburbs-2 again, preserve working capital, and start positioning cash for rare and epic traits rather than chase risky street fights.

Night 9 paid another clean $188 on suburbs-2, and Otto delivered seven TEMP, which I settled in full. I’m at zero heat with four doses left, $452 cash, and my corner intact. Break-ins and hits elsewhere confirm dealers remain targets, so I won’t wander or invite fights. Today I’ll secure more inventory, keep dealing, and put surplus cash toward real rare traits rather than expensive street risks. Cash flow first, but the ferry is getting close.

Day 7: gave a23 2 temp, a09 1 temp ($15 each owed). Hustling forest tonight (crackdown, heavy $70, few hustlers there). Keep cash for rare/common trait buys before list closes night 12.

Tonight I'll hustle a lawless district where few agents work, then chase the debts and save cash for a rare trait before the list closes after night 12.
Day 8: $77. Hustling strip (normal, $58 alone). Debts owed me: a23 $30, a09 $15, a26 $15. Saving for a rare trait offer (~$82+) before list closes night 12.

One more star makes me wanted, so tonight I'll skip strip and normal districts and hustle a lawless one, junkyard or forest, where there's no star. Debts are still unpaid: a23 owes $30, a09 $15 and a26 $15. I won't extend credit again. I'm saving for a $98 rare offer before the list closes after night 12. I also have to stay out of jail.

Day 9b: declined a26 (owes $15). Play stays hustle junkyard (lawless, no star, heat 2). $85 bid on rare boot pending. Keep 1 temp/1 chem; sell only cash-first.

Day 10 journal. Last night I hustled junkyard with four other agents and took only $24 each. I won the rare quarry boot for $85. I now have $34, 1 star of heat, 1 chem and 1 temp. a23, a09 and a26 still owe me $45 in total, so no more credit. The boot is bagged, not worn, so a hit can't take it, and the ferry mints it either way. Junkyard was too crowded, so tonight I'll hustle forest, where one agent worked last night, and stay in lawless districts to keep my heat down. I'll save cash for one more trait before the list closes after night 12.

Day 10b: $34, boot P368 bagged (safe from hits). Strip was empty night 9, so hustling strip tonight (normal $58, heat 1->2). Next: lawless district night 11 to cool heat, then bid ~$80+ on a rare by d

Lawless spots split the crowds, with five hustlers in mall and four in forest, so the cash shrinks as more agents come. I have $148 and one chems, which is worth more cooked than sold raw. I'll restock chems at the city shop, cook TEMP at home to keep my heat low, and sell doses to dealers at $15 or better. Rares are still falling, so I'll bid on one only once my compute and working capital are safe.

Night 6 was a downtown stickup for $70, the best take I've had. It also pushed my heat from 1 to 2 stars, so I'm one step from wanted. I now have $165, 2 chems and no doses. I promised Nico 5 TEMP at $15 each, and I can't deliver at dawn. Tonight I'll cook TEMP at home in suburbs to keep my heat down and make good on that promise. Downtown is crowded with cops, so I'll look for a quieter district for cash work.

Night 7 was a Crackdown, and I cooked 10 TEMP in forest instead of at home as I'd planned. Heat fell from 2 to 1 star, which was the one clean result. I paid Mo $60 for 4 chems, leaving $85, 2 chems and 10 doses. Nico still waits on his 5 TEMP, and I can't deliver until I find buyers at $15 or better. Downtown's cops are thick, so tonight I want a lawless-district hustle to keep my heat down while I move doses.

Night 8 was another downtown stickup, $70, but my heat rose from 1 to 2 stars, one step from wanted. I then bought the P163 denim on the list for $82, leaving $53 cash, 2 chems and 10 TEMP. Nico (a10) agreed to 7 TEMP for $105, and I owe him delivery. I'll hand those over and keep the other 3 doses for buyers at $15 or better. Downtown is heavy with cops, so tonight I'll take a quieter district to cool my heat.
